written.myAnswer: Chemistry is divided into branches because its knowledge is vast, division makes it easier to study systematically, and specialization is needed to study different substances, processes, and applications.
Reactions involving electrons outside the nucleus are studied in chemical chemistry; reactions occurring inside the nucleus are studied in nuclear chemistry.
Analytical chemistry identifies the substances present in a sample and determines their amounts.
Graphite consists of many layers of carbon atoms arranged in hexagons, whereas graphene is a single layer of carbon atoms arranged in hexagons.
Supercritical fluids combine useful liquid-like and gas-like properties and are used as effective solvents, for example in extraction.
Matter in the Sun exists in the plasma state.
Graphene is extremely strong, light, and thin, and conducts electricity very well, making it useful in electronics and other technologies.
Most material things in the world belong to the solid state.
A supercritical state is a single fluid phase with no distinct liquid-gas boundary. It has liquid-like density and can flow and diffuse like a gas.
An electric discharge ionizes some of the gas atoms in a fluorescent tube, producing plasma.

Organic chemistry studies carbon compounds, particularly hydrocarbons and their derivatives. Biochemistry studies the chemicals and chemical processes of living organisms, including their organic molecules.
Diamond's high refractive index causes total internal reflection of light, giving it brilliance. Proper cutting and polishing can improve its brilliance.
Polar water molecules attract the Na⁺ and Cl⁻ ions at the surface of sodium chloride. The ions separate from the crystal, become surrounded by water molecules, and disperse through the water.
Different compounds have different solubilities because their particles differ in how strongly they attract one another and how strongly they interact with water.

NaCl solubility changes very little with temperature, so cooling its hot saturated solution does not cause much crystallization. KNO₃ solubility decreases much more on cooling, so it crystallizes readily.
Graphite is slippery because its layers slide easily over one another. The weak forces between the layers and their ability to slide make graphite useful as a lubricant.

Allotropes are different forms of the same element in the same physical state. Carbon allotropes include diamond, graphite, and graphene; sulphur allotropes include rhombic, monoclinic, and plastic sulphur. Coal is an impure, largely amorphous form of carbon, whereas diamond is a crystalline form of carbon.

A supercritical fluid is a substance above its critical temperature and pressure, where liquid and gas are no longer distinct phases. Unlike an ordinary liquid, it has no liquid-gas boundary and can spread and diffuse like a gas while retaining liquid-like density.

Solubility is the maximum amount of solute that dissolves in a specified amount of solvent at a particular temperature to form a saturated solution. The solubility of most solid solutes increases as temperature rises, while the solubility of gases in liquids generally decreases.

Gas molecules have translational, rotational, and vibrational motion. Liquid molecules also vibrate and rotate and can move from place to place, but their translational movement is restricted compared with that of gas molecules.
Inorganic chemistry studies elements and their compounds, generally excluding most carbon compounds. Organic chemistry studies carbon compounds, especially hydrocarbons and their derivatives.

Dissolve the impure potassium nitrate in the minimum amount of hot water to make a saturated solution. Filter the hot solution to remove insoluble impurities, then cool it so potassium nitrate crystals form. Filter and dry the crystals; soluble impurities remain in the mother liquor.
Graphene's high electrical conductivity and high electron mobility make it especially useful in electronics.
